Banks, The Fed And A Trailblazing BoJ

Louis-Vincent Gave

Gavekal Research | 30 Jul 2026

Over the past 30 years, the Bank of Japan has almost always been the first to engage in what could best be described as unconventional monetary policy. The BoJ was the first major central bank to embrace zero interest rate policies, the first to embrace quantitative easing, the first to embrace negative interest rate policies… and with each of these steps, the rest of the world typically looked on with surprise, and sometimes even disgust at the Japanese central bankers’ actions. In this spirit of unconventional policies, over the past few years, the BoJ has sat on its hands as inflation accelerated and the long end of the Japanese government bond market sold off.
